title: Palmer Penguins Analysis with Python
text:
This post is to practice skills learned in DSCI 521 including github pages, uv, renv and venv as well as quatro.
This post explores differences in body mass and flipper length among penguin species.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt 
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins




df_peng = load_penguins()
df_peng.head()

#grouping by species to investigate flipper length and body mass 
species_summary = df_peng.groupby("species").agg(
    avg_body_mass = ("body_mass_g", "mean"),
    avg_flipper_length = ("flipper_length_mm", "mean")
).reset_index()





species_summary.plot(
    x="species",
    y="avg_body_mass",
    kind="bar"
)

plt.ylabel("Average Body Mass (g)")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.title("Avg Body Mass by Species")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Average body mass of Palmer penguins by species.





Gentoo are heaviest species on average while Adelie and Chinstrap are tied.
#Flipper Length and Body Mass Correlation

plt.scatter(
    df_peng["flipper_length_mm"],
    df_peng["body_mass_g"]
)

plt.xlabel("Flipper Length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body Mass (g)")
plt.title("Avg Flipper Length vs Body Mass")
plt.show()







Figure 2: Relationship between flipper length and body mass in Palmer penguins.





According to plot 2 body mass and flipper length are postively correlated.

title: Palmer Penguins with R and Python
text:
This post demonstrates interoperability between R and Python using reticulate. R is used to create a summary of the Palmer Penguins dataset, and the resulting object is passed to Python for further analysis.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(reticulate)


species_summary <- penguins |>
    group_by(species) |>
    summarise(
        avg_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
        avg_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

species_summary

# A tibble: 3 × 3
  species   avg_body_mass avg_flipper_length
  <fct>             <dbl>              <dbl>
1 Adelie            3701.               190.
2 Chinstrap         3733.               196.
3 Gentoo            5076.               217.

title: Palmer Penguins with R and Python
section: Passing the R Summary to Python
text:
Passing the R Summary to Python
The species_summary object was created in R. The following Python code accesses this R object using reticulate and uses it for further analysis.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

summary_python = r.species_summary

summary_python

     species  avg_body_mass  avg_flipper_length
0     Adelie    3700.662252          189.953642
1  Chinstrap    3733.088235          195.823529
2     Gentoo    5076.016260          217.186992



plt.bar(
    summary_python["species"],
    summary_python["avg_body_mass"]
)

plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Average Body Mass (g)")
plt.title("R Summary Visualized with Python")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Average body mass plotted in Python using summary data created in R.





#| label: fig-r-flipper-mass #| fig-cap: “Relationship between flipper length and body mass in Palmer penguins.”
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + labs( x = “Flipper Length (mm)”, y = “Body Mass (g)”, title = “Flipper Length vs Body Mass” )
The scatterplot shows a positive association between body mass and flipper length. Penguins with longer flippers generally have greater body mass.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day on campus.


My first week in the UBC Master of Data Science (MDS) Vancouver program has been an exciting introduction to what promises to be an intense and rewarding year. The first few days focused on getting familiar with the program, meeting my classmates and instructors, and adjusting to the pace of the coursework. There is already a lot to learn, but it has been great to finally begin the program and start working with the tools and concepts that will form the foundation of the months ahead.
During the first week, we began working across several areas of data science, including programming, statistics, data manipulation, and version control. I have been getting more comfortable working with Python and R while also learning how Git and GitHub fit into a collaborative data science workflow. The hands-on labs and assignments have made it clear that the program will require a lot of practice and problem-solving rather than simply learning concepts in isolation.
Overall, my first week at UBC MDS has been challenging but encouraging. There have already been moments where I have had to troubleshoot code, learn unfamiliar tools, and rethink concepts that initially seemed confusing. At the same time, each problem I solve makes me a little more comfortable with the data science workflow. This is only the beginning, and I am looking forward to seeing how much my technical skills and understanding of data science develop throughout the program.

This post explores differences in body mass and flipper length among penguin species using R.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)




penguins |>

# ℹ 2 more variables: sex <fct>, year <int>



species_summary <- penguins |>
   dplyr :: group_by(species) |>
   dplyr :: summarise(
        avg_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
        avg_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

species_summary

  <fct>             <dbl>              <dbl>

Genboo is heaviest on average then tie between Chinstrap and Adelie.
